entry.title: How a Nonprofit Built a 24/7 Cancer Support Agent To Save Lives | Testicular Cancer Foundation

media:group.media:title: How a Nonprofit Built a 24/7 Cancer Support Agent To Save Lives | Testicular Cancer Foundation
media:group.media:description:
When someone finds a lump at 2 AM, they're scared, they're alone, and they're not ready to talk to anyone yet.
The Testicular Cancer Foundation built something for that moment. The TC Navigator is an AI agent live on testicularcancer.org, built on Chatbase by a team of fewer than 10 people. It went from idea to deployed in under an hour, using clinical content TCF had already spent a year building.
The Navigator isn't replacing TCF's team. It's the on-ramp. Men work through the hard questions anonymously first, get to a point of comfort, then reach out to a human already informed and a little less afraid. If you run a nonprofit or mission-driven org and you're wondering whether AI fits your work, this is what it can look like: not a glorified FAQ, but a support layer that shows up when your people can't.
What happened next:
→ 484 questions answered in the first few days → 60 conversations handled with zero staff typing a word → Patients reached across 12 countries, 28% from outside the US → Automatic language detection in Portuguese, Turkish, German, and Spanish → One survivor sent 157 messages in a single session, cross-referencing his own imaging against clinical guidelines
Hear from Kenny Kane (CEO) on what they built, why it worked, and what the data surfaced that no survey ever could.
Learn more about Chatbase → chatbase.co Learn more about the TCF → testicularcancer.org
